key_insight: Human and LLM collaboration can accelerate materials synthesis by producing experimentally testable recipes, with comparable success on known materials and modest but real discovery of new ones.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that closed-loop human/LLM workflows can be used to prioritize synthesis targets and shorten the path from candidate generation to lab validation in materials engineering.
method: Generated synthesis recipes with both humans and an LLM for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials.
Tested the recipes through in-lab experimentation and fed results back into a closed loop.
Compared success rates across two rounds to assess learning and collaboration effects.
evidence_signal: In-lab evaluation showed similar success on known materials (83% vs 75% in round one; 79% vs 71% in round two) but much lower success on unknown materials, with one new material discovered: Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply for unknown targets, so recipe generation still requires careful experimental screening and cannot replace domain expertise.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
